title: [cupertino_ui] CupertinoListTile: add `enabled`
body:
### Use case iOS greys out a disabled list row, in UIKit and SwiftUI. `CupertinoListTile` can only drop `onTap`, which leaves the row looking tappable. A `null` `onTap` can't mean disabled either, since iOS leaves rows with nothing to tap as they are. ### Proposal `enabled`, like `ListTile.enabled`. When `false`: no tap, `title` in `tertiaryLabel`, `subtitle` and `additionalInfo` in `quaternaryLabel`. Those are the colours UIKit's list cells switch to on iOS 18.5 and 26.2.
UIKit ```swift var content = UIListContentConfiguration.valueCell() content.text = "Wi-Fi" content.secondaryText = "On" cell.contentConfiguration = content cell.isUserInteractionEnabled = false ```
The slider has the same gap: #106691.
